relations.myth: Joint receipt of Bellausus’s vow at Sarrebourg
relations.note: They appear together as paired figures receiving Bellausus’s votive dedication.
Modern scholarship conventionally interprets the securely paired goddess as Sucellus’s consort or parèdre.
Dedications explicitly conjoin or fuse Sucellus with the Roman rural god Silvanus.
A Mainz dedication locally assimilates Sucaelus to Jupiter Best and Greatest.

relations.myth: Joint receipt of the Mainz dedication
relations.note: The local Genius receives a dedication alongside Jupiter Optimus Maximus Sucaelus.
Diana appears beside some wider mallet-god figures conditionally identified as Sucellus.
Silvana accompanies male figures in the wider corpus, though their Sucellus identity is uncertain.

relations.myth: Proserpina paired with an attributed mallet-god
relations.note: Some catalogues pair her with a mallet-god tentatively identified as Sucellus.

relations.myth: The pair walk and order a young world
relations.note: Contemporary devotional myths make them order nature, teach agriculture, and protect households.
An online cosmology claims Eenatun created a female version of Sucellus.
A modern cosmology makes Sucellus act with Dea Patrono as co-creators.

relations.myth: Creation by Sucellus and Dea Patrono
relations.note: A modern cosmology claims Sucellus and Dea Patrono created Taranis.

relations.myth: Creation by Sucellus and Dea Patrono
relations.note: A modern cosmology claims Sucellus and Dea Patrono created Cernunnos.
